passages.text: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is Solomon.  
Solomon speaks to his beloved.  
Solomon calls his beloved beautiful.  
He says, "You are beautiful, my darling."  
He repeats, "You are beautiful."  
He says, "Your eyes are like doves."  
He says, "Your eyes are behind your veil."  
He says, "Your hair is like a flock of goats."  
He says, "The goats stream down Mount Gilead."
passages.original: הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ הִנָּ֣ךְ יָפָ֔ה עֵינַ֣יִךְ יוֹנִ֔ים מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵ֑ךְ שַׂעְרֵךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שֶׁגָּלְשׁ֖וּ מֵהַ֥ר גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He describes her teeth.
Her teeth are white and clean.
They are like a flock of sheep.
The sheep have just been shorn.
The sheep have come up from washing.
Each tooth has a matching pair.
None of her teeth are missing.
passages.original: שִׁנַּ֙יִךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הַקְּצוּב֔וֹת שֶׁעָל֖וּ מִן־ הָרַחְצָ֑ה שֶׁכֻּלָּם֙ מַתְאִימ֔וֹת וְשַׁכֻּלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who loves a woman deeply.
He speaks to his beloved.
He says, "Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon."
He says, "Your mouth is lovely."
He says, "Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate."
passages.original: כְּח֤וּט הַשָּׁנִי֙ שִׂפְתֹתַ֔יִךְ וּמִדְבָּרֵ֖יךְ נָאוֶ֑ה כְּפֶ֤לַח הָֽרִמּוֹן֙ רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
passages.sermon:
The woman is beautiful and flawless.
Her neck is strong and graceful.
Her neck is like the tower of David.
The tower of David stands tall and firm.
Builders made the tower with rows of stones.
A thousand shields hang on the tower.
These shields belong to mighty warriors.
passages.original: כְּמִגְדַּ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ צַוָּארֵ֔ךְ בָּנ֖וּי לְתַלְפִּיּ֑וֹת אֶ֤לֶף הַמָּגֵן֙ תָּל֣וּי עָלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל שִׁלְטֵ֥י הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who loves a woman deeply.
He describes the woman’s body with gentle words.
He says, “Your breasts are like two fawns.”
These fawns are twins of a gazelle.
The fawns graze among the lilies.
The man uses this image to show beauty, gentleness, and innocence.
passages.original: שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תְּאוֹמֵ֣י צְבִיָּ֑ה הָרוֹעִ֖ים בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃

passages.text: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who loves his bride.
He speaks to his beloved.
He says, “Before the day breaks, I will go.”
He says, “Before the shadows disappear, I will go.”
He will go to the mountain of myrrh.
He will go to the hill of frankincense.
passages.original: עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֙וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים אֵ֤לֶךְ לִי֙ אֶל־ הַ֣ר הַמּ֔וֹר וְאֶל־ גִּבְעַ֖ת הַלְּבוֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He calls her "my darling."
He says she is completely beautiful.
He sees no flaw in her.
passages.original: כֻּלָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י וּמ֖וּם אֵ֥ין בָּֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a bridegroom.
He speaks to his bride.
He calls her to come with him.
He says, "Come with me from Lebanon, my bride."
He repeats, "Come with me from Lebanon."
He tells her to descend from the peak of Amana.
He tells her to come down from the summits of Senir and Hermon.
He calls her to leave the dens of the lions.
He calls her to leave the mountains of the leopards.
passages.original: אִתִּ֤י מִלְּבָנוֹן֙ כַּלָּ֔ה אִתִּ֖י מִלְּבָנ֣וֹן תָּב֑וֹאִי תָּשׁ֣וּרִי׀ מֵרֹ֣אשׁ אֲמָנָ֗ה מֵרֹ֤אשׁ שְׂנִיר֙ וְחֶרְמ֔וֹן מִמְּעֹנ֣וֹת אֲרָי֔וֹת מֵֽהַרְרֵ֖י נְמֵרִֽים׃

passages.text: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who loves a woman deeply.
He calls her "my sister" and "my bride."
He says, "You have captured my heart."
He says, "You have stolen my heart."
He explains how she did this.
He says, "You did it with one glance of your eyes."
He says, "You did it with one jewel on your neck."
passages.original: לִבַּבְתִּ֖נִי אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה לִבַּבְתִּ֙ינִי֙ בְּאַחַד מֵעֵינַ֔יִךְ בְּאַחַ֥ד עֲנָ֖ק מִצַּוְּרֹנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He calls her "my sister" and "my bride."
He says her love is delightful.
He says her love is better than wine.
He says the fragrance of her perfume is better than all spices.
passages.original: מַה־ יָּפ֥וּ דֹדַ֖יִךְ אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה מַה־ טֹּ֤בוּ דֹדַ֙יִךְ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן וְרֵ֥יחַ שְׁמָנַ֖יִךְ מִכָּל־ בְּשָׂמִֽים׃

passages.text: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his bride.
He calls her "my bride."
He says her lips drip with sweetness.
Her lips are as sweet as honeycomb.
Honey is under her tongue.
Milk is under her tongue.
Her garments have a pleasant fragrance.
The fragrance of her garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.
passages.original: נֹ֛פֶת תִּטֹּ֥פְנָה שִׂפְתוֹתַ֖יִךְ כַּלָּ֑ה דְּבַ֤שׁ וְחָלָב֙ תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְרֵ֥יחַ שַׂלְמֹתַ֖יִךְ כְּרֵ֥יחַ לְבָנֽוֹן׃ס

passages.text: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He calls her "my sister" and "my bride."
She is precious to him.
She is like a garden that is locked.
No one can enter this garden.
She is like a spring that is enclosed.
No one can reach this spring.
She is like a fountain that is sealed.
No one can open this fountain.
passages.original: גַּ֥ן׀ נָע֖וּל אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה גַּ֥ל נָע֖וּל מַעְיָ֥ן חָתֽוּם׃

passages.text: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard, with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
passages.sermon:
The beloved speaks to his bride.
He describes her beauty and character.
He says her branches are like an orchard of pomegranates.
This orchard has the choicest fruits.
Her branches include henna and nard.
They also have nard and saffron.
There is calamus and cinnamon.
There are all kinds of frankincense trees.
There is myrrh and aloes.
There are all the finest spices.
passages.original: שְׁלָחַ֙יִךְ֙ פַּרְדֵּ֣ס רִמּוֹנִ֔ים עִ֖ם פְּרִ֣י מְגָדִ֑ים כְּפָרִ֖ים עִם־ נְרָדִֽים׃ נֵ֣רְדְּ׀ וְכַרְכֹּ֗ם קָנֶה֙ וְקִנָּמ֔וֹן עִ֖ם כָּל־ עֲצֵ֣י לְבוֹנָ֑ה מֹ֚ר וַאֲהָל֔וֹת עִ֖ם כָּל־ רָאשֵׁ֥י בְשָׂמִֽים׃

passages.text: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.
passages.sermon:
The woman is the beloved bride.
She is like a spring in a garden.
She is a well filled with living water.
Fresh water flows from her.
This water comes down from Lebanon.
passages.original: מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֣יִם חַיִּ֑ים וְנֹזְלִ֖ים מִן־ לְבָנֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman who loves her beloved.
She calls to the north wind.
She says, "Awake, north wind."
She calls to the south wind.
She says, "Come, south wind."
She asks the winds to blow on her garden.
She wants the winds to spread the scent of her spices.
She invites her beloved to enter the garden.
She wants her beloved to eat the best fruits in the garden.
passages.original: ע֤וּרִי צָפוֹן֙ וּב֣וֹאִי תֵימָ֔ן הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י יִזְּל֣וּ בְשָׂמָ֑יו יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל פְּרִ֥י מְגָדָֽיו׃
